items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Terminology 129:1
items.html: (To the question) What is the firmament? The Yesod of ZA is called the firmament, because the Yesod is the end of ZA, which separates the aspect of the lights of the world of the male, so that they do not illuminate from it and onward; and therefore it is discerned as the firmament that separates between the upper waters, which are male, and the lower waters, which are female, for from it and below the world of the Nukva begins. And upon the screen in this Yesod, which separates the illumination of the male, a coupling of striking takes place there with the Upper Light, since it pushes back the Upper Light from spreading through it, and therefore it raises the returning light. (Item 79).
